judgments.justification: The proposal restricts an averaging ensemble to quadratic-residue survivor primes and adds a variance/concentration objective on the solution-count function. This is an analytic moment-method move, not a passage from residue-class covering to a global integer/lattice representation, and it contains no lattice-point, integral-point, or enumeration argument and no mapping into a representation space. It honestly concedes that even success would not prove per-prime existence.
mathematical_objections: The claim that comparable restricted mean plus controlled variance would tightly bound the fraction of zero-solution primes is asserted as a hypothesis without any stated mechanism for converting second-moment control into pointwise existence; Chebyshev-type bounds cannot exclude a sparse zero set without much stronger tail information than is described.
unresolved: Whether the sieve estimates invoked remain valid on the thinner survivor-class ensemble is not determinable from the text.
What concentration strength would actually be needed to constrain zero-solution primes is not quantified.

judgments.justification: This proposal is a restricted-class higher-moment and concentration study of the solution-count function f(p). It stays entirely within the statistical/averaging mechanism family: there is no global integer or lattice representation of solutions, no lattice-point counting or enumeration argument, and no positivity/integrality/coverage mapping of the kind the criterion requires. Its uncertainty is stated honestly but the synthetic mechanism is different in kind.
mathematical_objections: The suggestion that moment concentration could make a zero-solution prime 'inconsistent' is not supported by any stated mechanism; moments over an ensemble cannot by themselves contradict a single exceptional prime unless an effectively pointwise input is added, which the proposal does not identify.
unresolved: Whether second and higher moments of f(p) on the survivor class are actually computable with current sieve technology is not assessable from the text.

judgments.justification: This is a meta-level program: formalize method families and map the exact boundary of the reciprocity obstruction, proving for each family that it either reduces to fixed-modulus congruence data or escapes. It proposes no representation of solutions at all, global or otherwise, and no existence, lattice-point, or enumeration argument; its deliverable is a classification of which mechanisms are already blocked. It does not attempt the criterion's synthetic move.
mathematical_objections: The predicate 'reduces to fixed-modulus congruence data' is left informal; without a precise definition the claimed dichotomy (blocked vs. escaping) may not be well-posed, and the proposal itself flags that the existence of a sharp provable boundary is only a hypothesis.
unresolved: Which concrete method families would be formalized, and in what formal language the reduction would be stated, cannot be determined from the text.

judgments.justification: The proposal does make a move toward a global arithmetic representation: solutions for survivor primes would inject into representation data of binary quadratic forms or class-group invariants, with existence inherited from independently known positivity of class numbers or representation counts. Quadratic-form representation numbers are lattice-theoretic objects, so this is adjacent to the intended representation-plus-positivity mechanism. However, no mapping is described even in outline — the proposal states that constructing a faithful correspondence is 'the entire unmet obligation' — and the positivity, integrality, and coverage obligations are named only abstractly, so the concrete lattice-point/existence argument the criterion requires is absent.
mathematical_objections: No candidate discriminant or correspondence is specified, so faithfulness (injectivity on the survivor class) and the direction of the positivity transfer are unverifiable; positivity of a class number does not by itself yield positivity of the fiber of an unspecified map.
The positivity of the auxiliary invariant being 'independently known' does not address the integrality and positivity constraints on the unit-fraction denominators x, y, z themselves.
unresolved: Which auxiliary discriminants would be n-dependent candidates, and whether any natural correspondence exists even for small primes, cannot be determined from the text.

judgments.justification: This is an empirical pattern-mining direction: extract non-congruence denominator parameterizations from certified solutions of quadratic-residue primes in the verified range and test extrapolation on held-out instances. The mechanism is data-driven rule fitting over solved instances, with no global integer or lattice representation of the solution set and no lattice-point or enumeration existence argument. It does not attempt the criterion's move.
unresolved: Whether the verification data actually retains full solution certificates (rather than existence bits) for survivor primes is assumed but not verifiable from the text.
What class of candidate rules would be admitted, and how 'not expressible as a fixed-modulus congruence' would be certified for a fitted rule, is unspecified.

judgments.justification: The proposal keeps the classical two-unit-fraction reduction but makes the choice of the first denominator x adaptive to the individual divisor structure of n instead of its residue class. This is a refinement of an existing constructive reduction — the representation remains the two-fraction split and divisor analysis of 4/n − 1/x — and it contains no global lattice representation and no lattice-point counting or enumeration argument. The criterion's synthetic move is not attempted.
mathematical_objections: The proposal seeks a criterion under which an admissible x 'always exists' for square-like n but offers no candidate structural mechanism for why divisor-adaptive selection should evade the survivor-class hardness that defeats class-keyed selection; the escape from the obstruction is asserted as unconstrained rather than argued.
unresolved: Whether the reciprocity obstruction extends to divisor-adaptive selection is explicitly left open and cannot be resolved from the text.

judgments.justification: The proposal relocates the search to a global algebraic object — the unifying higher-dimensional variety — and seeks rational slices not derived from congruence identities, which is a genuine step away from independent residue-class covering toward a global representation. However, the existence mechanism remains slice/parameterization search: there is no integral-point or lattice-point counting argument on that representation, and the positivity and integrality obligations for solutions arising from a found slice are never stated. It captures the re-representation half of the intended move but not the concrete lattice-point/existence argument.
mathematical_objections: The hypothesis that a wall-crossing polynomial-style construction 'must' appear as a rational slice of this particular variety is unjustified; the variety unifies known parameterizations and there is no stated reason it is universal for all polynomial constructions.
Coverage via a slice would still require its specializations to hit every survivor prime, an obligation the proposal does not articulate.
unresolved: The variety itself is never described concretely enough to assess whether 'rational slice' is well-defined for it or whether the proposed congruence-reducibility test is decidable.

judgments.justification: This is a descent/induction mechanism: transport solutions from solved smaller instances to hard primes via induced-solution maps, ordered by a monovariant. The representation is a relational graph on instances, not a global integer or lattice representation of the solution set, and existence would come from well-founded recursion, not from lattice-point counting or enumeration. It is candid that the transport map and monovariant are entirely open, but the synthetic mechanism is a different one from the criterion's.
mathematical_objections: No candidate induced-solution map with even heuristic monovariant decrease is exhibited, and the proposal itself concedes this; without one, the well-foundedness requirement is vacuous.
unresolved: Which induced-solution relations from the structural analysis are actually functional (defined for every survivor prime) cannot be determined from the text.

judgments.justification: This proposal is an adversarial empirical stress test of the Type A/B completeness conjecture: classify certified solutions of survivor primes and hunt for a prime whose solutions avoid both forms. It is a challenge/falsification operation on an existing congruence-form classification, not a move to a global integer or lattice representation, and it contains no existence or lattice-point argument. It explicitly scopes its output as an empirical finding.
unresolved: Whether the Type A/B forms are checkable from solution certificates alone (rather than requiring re-derivation of the congruence data) is assumed but not demonstrable from the text.

judgments.justification: This proposal makes precisely the intended synthetic move: it passes from class-based identity/covering mechanisms to a global representation — fibers of the lifted unifying variety over each fixed n — and proposes a concrete lattice-point argument, counting integral points in explicitly described bounded fiber regions with a geometry-of-numbers estimate and an effective positivity bound. It states the mapping (fiber integral points correspond to solutions), the integrality object (integral points), the positivity obligation (main term must beat error terms on thin fibers), and the coverage stance (applied per survivor prime with no residue restriction), rather than merely invoking 'lattice' as vocabulary. It also honestly records that the lift is known to add no positivity by itself.
mathematical_objections: The correspondence between integral points of the fiber region and valid positive solution triples (x, y, z) is assumed, not exhibited; the mapping's faithfulness, and in particular the positivity of the recovered denominators, is an unverified obligation and must not be treated as established.

Fibers over fixed n are thin (roughly dimension-2 slices of an affine hypersurface condition), so a naive volume main term may be ill-defined or dominated by boundary/error terms; the proposal acknowledges this battle but gives no reason the main term is even asymptotically positive on survivor primes.
unresolved: The explicit description of the fiber regions — and whether they are convex or otherwise amenable to standard geometry-of-numbers tools — cannot be determined from the text.
Whether the counting would be uniform in p, which coverage of every survivor prime requires, is not addressed.

judgments.justification: This proposal replaces congruence-class coverage with dynamical orbit coverage: propagate known solutions through induced-solution maps and ask whether the orbit of the solved set reaches every survivor prime. The representation is an orbit/reachability structure on instances, not a global integer or lattice representation of solutions, and there is no lattice-point counting or enumeration existence argument. The move is genuinely away from fixed-modulus covering, but toward a different mechanism than the criterion's.
mathematical_objections: Whether the induced maps' reach escapes the residue/non-residue dichotomy is posed as open, but no structural property of any specific map is offered that would make escape plausible; if the maps are algebraically defined by fixed relations, their images may themselves be congruence-constrained.
unresolved: The inventory of explicit induced-solution maps available from the structural analysis, and whether they act on primes at all (rather than only composite n), cannot be determined from the text.

judgments.justification: This proposal seeks a pointwise divisor-in-interval existence statement for quantities of the form x(4x − n), upgrading known average-case divisor-density results to every prime in the survivor class. Although it is a global-quantifier, per-prime existence argument, its representation is divisor structure of an auxiliary integer, not a global integer/lattice representation of the solution set, and it contains no lattice-point or enumeration mapping. It states its central obligation (average-to-pointwise upgrade) honestly, but the mechanism is multiplicative-divisor analysis rather than the criterion's move.
mathematical_objections: The average-to-pointwise upgrade it depends on is not merely unproven but is of a type known to fail in general (individual integers can lack divisors in prescribed intervals), and the proposal offers no structural reason survivor-class values of x(4x − n) should be exceptional; it acknowledges this openly.
unresolved: Which interval the two-fraction split actually requires, as a function of n and x, is not specified precisely enough to assess feasibility.

judgments.justification: This proposal indexes decomposition parameters by n-specific multiplicative data (e.g., a least-nonresidue witness) instead of by residue class to a fixed modulus, so that no finite congruence-class union describes the construction. It remains a constructive, formula-based parameterization mechanism — the representation is witness-indexed decompositions, not a global integer or lattice representation — and it proposes per-instance verification, not a lattice-point or enumeration existence argument. The criterion's synthetic move is not attempted.
mathematical_objections: No candidate witness-indexed formula is given, so the claim that the Jacobi-symbol forcing argument 'does not directly read' such parameterizations cannot be evaluated; the proposal itself flags that the obstruction may reappear in witness-indexed form.
unresolved: Whether bounds on the least quadratic nonresidue (conditional or unconditional) would be strong enough for any concrete construction is not determinable from the text.
